usage.callShape: POST https://httpay.xyz/api/gateway/supabase/rest/v1/<table> with header X-Upstream-Token: <your Supabase JWT/API key> and JSON body (PostgREST). REQUIRES caller-supplied upstream key — not callable without one.

inputExample._note: plus a PostgREST table path and body; bare /rest/v1/ root is not a valid PostgREST resource

usage.outputShape: untested — gateway never reaches a working Supabase response without a valid upstream key; demo returns body.error / body.message
quirks: HTTPay gateway: surface shows 402 (payable) but the upstream Supabase service REQUIRES a caller-supplied API key — paying does NOT make it work.

Verified FREE via ?demo=true (10 calls/IP/hr): POST /rest/v1/?demo=true returns 401 {error:'Service supabase requires authentication', instructions:'Pass your upstream API key via the X-Upstream-Token header'}.
With a fake X-Upstream-Token the upstream replies {message:'JWT could not be decoded'} — confirming a REAL Supabase project JWT is required; there is no shared keyless backend.
Target URL points at bare PostgREST /rest/v1/ root with no table — even with a key you must append a real table path; root is not a valid PostgREST resource.
Violates MasterKey no-API-key policy; recommend pruning this endpoint from the registry.
usage.guide: Do not use this endpoint as a keyless paid service — it is not one. The HTTPay '/api/gateway/supabase' route is a thin proxy to YOUR OWN Supabase project: it demands an X-Upstream-Token header containing a valid Supabase JWT/API key, and forwards to a Supabase REST URL you must also target with a real table path (the registered URL stops at bare /rest/v1/). Without a caller-supplied key it returns 401 'Service supabase requires authentication'; with a bad key the upstream returns 'JWT could not be decoded'. This was confirmed for free via the ?demo=true preview, so no USDC was spent. Because MasterKey's policy excludes endpoints needing a caller-supplied auth key, this should be dropped from the registry rather than tested.
